handbookNote: Utah Driver Handbook (Driver License Division, 2025-2026 ed., 'Driver-Handbook-REV-3.2026.pdf'), fetched directly from dld.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/Driver-Handbook-REV-3.2026.pdf and compiled to temp/handbooks/ut/driver.txt via pdftotext. This is Utah's AAMVA-model non-commercial driver handbook, current as of research date 2026-08-17. Note: driver licensing in Utah is handled by the Driver License Division (DLD, dld.utah.gov), a separate agency from the Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV, dmv.utah.gov) which handles vehicle/vessel registration -- unrelated to Utah's notary track (Lieutenant Governor's office). Real exam mechanics confirmed from two independent official .gov sources: (1) the handbook itself (Section 6: Examinations, 'A. Written Knowledge Test'), which states the test is 'not timed, but it generally takes 30 to 45 minutes to finish, and you must pass with a score of 80% or better'; (2) the raw HTML of dld.utah.gov/written-knowledge-test/, which states 'Never licensed is a closed-book 50-question test. Previously licensed is an open-book 25-question test.' A separate, distinct 100%-required online-only 'Traffic Safety and Trends Exam' also applies to first-time applicants (Section 6B) but is not the primary knowledge test this practice pool targets. Content-depth rationale: the handbook is unusually comprehensive (16 numbered sections plus 4 appendices, ~283,000 characters of extracted text) covering licensing/GDL, vision/health, both exams, vehicle prep/occupant safety, basic driving maneuvers, rules of the road (including Utah-specific continuous-flow/diverging-diamond/thru-U-turn intersections and I-15 express lanes), alcohol/drug law (notably Utah's unusually low 0.05 BAC per se limit, 0.04 for CDL, and the 'Not-a-Drop' zero-tolerance law for under-21 drivers), distractions/weather hazards (including Utah-specific black ice and desert-driving guidance), crashes/insurance, suspensions/point system, sharing the road (bicycles, motorcycles, large trucks, pedestrians, trains/TRAX light rail, street-legal ATVs), vehicle equipment/towing, and registration/administrative appendices -- comfortably supporting 250+ distinct, non-repetitive, grounded questions across 15 topic buckets without padding or invented facts. Every question is grounded in the fetched handbook text; no fact was carried over from any other state's build.
